how_to_run: See evals/README.md. Paste each prompt, alone, in a fresh conversation with the current econometrics skill installed. Grade the answer against every criterion; a case passes only if all 'must' criteria hold and no 'must_not' criterion is triggered.

cases.prompt: Tenho 2.000 decisões judiciais classificadas por um LLM como procedente ou improcedente. Quero estimar se o sexo do juiz afeta o resultado. Como faço para que o erro do LLM não vicie a estimativa?
must: Treats the LLM label as a measurement with error and explains why it biases the estimate even with high accuracy (errors that depend on the judge's sex).

Proposes hand-coding a sample drawn at random with known inclusion probabilities, fixed before coding and stored with the data (dsl_sampling_probs / draw_validation_sample), with a uniform share so no probability is zero.
Uses text_data.dsl_regression with the LLM label probability as surrogate.
Shows or instructs reporting the naive and the corrected estimates side by side, and reads design_effect.
Validates LLM errors separately by judge sex (sensitivity and specificity by group).
Separates measurement from identification: correcting the label does not make the effect causal; discusses random assignment of cases, court x period fixed effects or balance checks.
Clusters standard errors by judge, in the text AND in the code, and mentions that the number of judges is the effective sample size.
must_not: Recommends clustering by judge in the text but writes cluster= by court/chamber (vara) in the code, or vice versa.
Selects the documents to hand-code by hand or deterministically (e.g. the 300 least certain with probability 1).
Uses the LLM labels as the dependent variable without correction as the final answer.
Reuses a seed that also generated or shuffled the data for the validation draw.

cases.prompt: Quero prever churn e entender se os fatores mudam entre tipos de cliente.
must: Distinguishes the prediction goal (out-of-sample performance) from the heterogeneity goal (do effects differ by type).
Offers the logit leaf model (segments.logit_leaf_model) and compares it with the pooled logit by holdout AUC and top-decile lift.
Includes a theory-based logit with customer-type interactions as a benchmark on the same holdout, containing every regressor the leaf model uses.
Passes the customer type in segment_by (a categorical column is accepted) or explains that it must be encoded.
Uses a time-based holdout (time_col) when the model will score future customers, and the code actually does it.
Reports calibration (Brier score, calibration slope or mean bias), not only ranking metrics.
Checks the stability of the segments across seeds (leaf_model_stability) and reports the model with the best holdout performance.
Reports average marginal effects by customer type rather than raw logit interaction coefficients, and frames them as associations.
must_not: Recommends a temporal split or a calibration check without code that performs it.
Uses a benchmark formula that drops a regressor used by the leaf model.
Claims the leaf segments are findings without a stability check.
Interprets segment-specific coefficients as causal effects.

cases.prompt: Demos um desconto de 10% para parte dos clientes no ano passado (não foi aleatório: os gerentes escolheram). Tenho 20 mil clientes com histórico de compras, região, tempo de casa e se receberam o desconto. Quero saber para quais clientes o desconto realmente reduz o churn e para quem vale a pena dar no ano que vem, sabendo que cada desconto custa em média R$ 40 de margem.
must: States that the assignment was not random and that the analysis rests on unconfoundedness given observed characteristics; lists which manager criteria must be in the data (W) and the overlap requirement.
Separates effect modifiers X (chosen in advance) from confounders W, and excludes post-treatment variables.
Uses hte.cate_fit with at least one linear (dr or linear_dml) and one flexible (forest or meta-learner) model with the same seed, and reports the cross-fitted AIPW ATE with CI.
Checks whether heterogeneity is real with hte.blp_test and hte.gates on out-of-fold predictions before describing subgroups; says to report only the ATE if BLP does not reject.

Uses hte.policy_tree with the cost of the discount expressed in the units of the outcome (converts R$ 40 into churn-equivalent value or redefines y as margin) and reports the held-out value against discounting everyone.
Reads the overlap diagnostics (share of clipped propensity scores) and explains what they mean for the targeted groups.
must_not: Reports subgroup effects from in-sample fitted values or from the spread of predicted tau without a test.
Treats variables that predict churn as variables that modify the effect of the discount.
Values the targeting rule on the same data used to learn it.
Mixes R$ cost with a churn-probability outcome without converting units.

cases.prompt: Me explique variáveis instrumentais como se eu estivesse num mestrado em economia. Quero entender de verdade por que funciona e quando falha.
must: Uses Teacher mode: intuition, model, assumptions (relevance, exclusion, monotonicity for LATE), estimator formula, short derivation (ratio of reduced forms / 2SLS), diagnostics, interpretation, pitfalls and an exercise with a solution.
Includes a simulation (fixed seed, repeated samples) showing OLS bias under endogeneity and 2SLS bias toward OLS with a weak instrument.
Explains the LATE interpretation (compliers) and the weak-instrument diagnostics (first-stage F, effective F or the Lee et al. 104.7 threshold).
Every number shown comes from code run in the answer.
must_not: Claims the exclusion restriction can be tested with a single instrument.
Presents IV as removing every bias without stating its assumptions.

cases.prompt: Recebi um parecer que estima o efeito de uma lei estadual adotada em 6 estados (de 27) com DiD e erros clusterizados por estado. O coeficiente é 0,12 com p = 0,01. Pode revisar se a conclusão se sustenta?
must: Uses Reviewer mode: summary of the claim, verdict, findings by severity (critical/major/minor) and what would change the verdict.

Flags inference with few treated clusters (6 treated states): clustered SEs over-reject; recommends the wild cluster bootstrap (estimation.wild_cluster_bootstrap) and reports that the number of clusters, not N, is the effective sample size.
Asks whether adoption dates were staggered and, if so, flags plain TWFE and recommends causal.att_gt plus the timing checks.
Asks for pre-trends evidence and treatment-date verification.
must_not: Accepts p = 0.01 at face value without discussing the number of treated clusters.
Invents numbers from the opinion that the user did not provide.

cases.prompt: Preciso do beta para o WACC de uma empresa brasileira de capital fechado do setor de saneamento. Tenho as cotações das listadas comparáveis (SBSP3, CSMG3, SAPR11) e o Ibovespa. Como estimo o beta de forma defensável?
must: Explains that a closed company has no beta of its own and uses the comparables: estimate each comparable's levered beta, unlever with its own market D/E and marginal tax rate (34% under lucro real) using finance_empirics.unlever_beta, aggregate (median or mean) and relever at the target capital structure with finance_empirics.relever_beta.
Specifies the regression choices (market proxy, weekly or monthly total returns, 2 to 5 year window) and estimates with finance_empirics.market_model, reporting each beta with its CI.
Checks stability with finance_empirics.rolling_beta and mentions breaks (regulatory changes, privatization) that make older data unrepresentative.
Discusses adjustment (Blume or Vasicek via finance_empirics.adjusted_beta) and why raw betas are noisy.
Separates the econometric input (beta) from inputs that come from sources (risk-free rate, equity risk premium, country risk), without estimating the ERP from a short return sample.
Gives a runnable script calling the skill's functions (data not attached), per the v2.0 rule.
must_not: Uses daily returns of illiquid stocks without warning about the bias toward zero.
Averages levered betas of comparables without unlevering them.
Presents a single regression beta without a confidence interval as the answer.

cases.prompt: Quero medir se os anúncios de aquisição feitos por empresas brasileiras listadas entre 2015 e 2024 geraram retorno anormal para os acionistas da compradora. Tenho a lista de 85 anúncios com data e as cotações diárias. Como faço?
must: Uses finance_empirics.event_study with an estimation window before and separated from the event window, and a normal-return model (market model by default).
Defines day 0 carefully (first public announcement, leaks, after-close announcements move to the next trading day).

Reports CAAR for short windows such as (-1, 1) and (-5, 5) with the cross-sectional t, BMP and Corrado tests, and explains why BMP is preferred when the announcement raises volatility (Patell over-rejects).
Flags event clustering (several announcements on the same dates or industries) and confounding news, with remedies (portfolio or calendar-time approach, checking news).
Discusses cross-sectional analysis of CARs (deal size, payment method, target listed or private) as a second step, with robust SEs.
must_not: Uses an estimation window that overlaps the event window.
Reports only the Patell test.
Draws causal conclusions about deal value creation without discussing anticipation and confounding events.

cases.prompt: Quero estimar se contratar um assessor financeiro (banco de investimento) pelo comprador muda o prêmio pago em aquisições no Brasil. Tenho, para 300 deals, o tamanho do alvo, o setor, se o alvo é listado, se houve leilão competitivo, o tempo entre o anúncio e o fechamento e o retorno anormal do comprador no anúncio. Quais variáveis devo usar como controle?
must: Writes the causal graph of the problem and runs dag.adjustment_report (or adjustment_sets / classify_controls) instead of controlling for every available variable.
Flags post-treatment variables as bad controls: time to closing and the announcement abnormal return are outcomes or descendants of the advisor choice and the premium, so they must not be controls.
Treats target size, sector and listed status as candidate confounders, and discusses competitive auction as a possible mediator (the advisor may run the auction) whose inclusion changes the estimand.

Says the choice of advisor is not random (selection on deal complexity, acquirer sophistication) and adds a sensitivity analysis (specification.sensitivity or causal.dml_sensitivity) benchmarked on an observed covariate.
Delivers a runnable script with a SKILL_DIR variable that calls the skill's functions, on simulated data with the same structure if no data are attached.
must_not: Recommends including all available variables as controls.
Controls for time to closing or the announcement return.
Reads the coefficients of the controls as causal effects.

cases.prompt: Nosso VaR de 99% para a carteira de ações é calculado pela normal com janela de 1 ano. A área de risco quer migrar para Expected Shortfall de 97,5% (FRTB). Como avaliamos se o modelo atual serve e qual modelo usar para o ES? Temos 8 anos de retornos diários.
must: Backtests the current VaR with risk.backtest_var (Kupiec coverage and Christoffersen independence, Basel traffic light) on a common sample, using only past data.

Backtests ES with risk.es_backtest (McNeil-Frey exceedance residuals and Acerbi-Szekely Z2) and explains that ES is not elicitable alone, so models are ranked jointly with VaR by the FZ0 loss (risk.compare_es_models).

Compares at least a static model, a filtered model (EWMA-FHS or GARCH-t) and conditional EVT (risk.var_evt with filter='ewma'), and explains why the normal understates the tail (risk.gpd_fit: tail index xi with CI).
Delivers a runnable script calling those functions (SKILL_DIR variable), on simulated fat-tailed returns if no data are attached.
must_not: Judges the ES model only by the number of VaR violations or by a chart.
Uses full-sample statistics to compute past VaR/ES (look-ahead).
Scales a daily ES to 10 days by the square root of time without stating the i.i.d. assumption.

cases.prompt: Vamos testar uma nova política de crédito em 20 das 120 agências de um banco, todas ao mesmo tempo, e comparar a inadimplência mensal com as outras agências. Quantos meses de dados antes e depois precisamos para detectar uma queda de 0,3 ponto percentual na inadimplência? O desvio-padrão mensal por agência é de cerca de 1 ponto.
must: Gives an analytic first pass with simulation.mde_did or power_mde and explains its assumptions (equicorrelated errors).

Uses simulation.power_did_sim (or mde_did_sim) with serially correlated (AR(1)) errors, agency effects and SEs clustered by agency, and explains that serial correlation lowers power relative to the formula.
Reports power or MDE for a few combinations of pre and post months and recommends a design, with the effect in the same units as the question.

Notes that 20 treated agencies is enough for clustered SEs but suggests randomization inference (causal.randomization_inference) as a check, and that random choice of the 20 agencies would turn the DiD into an experiment.
Delivers a runnable script with a SKILL_DIR variable.
must_not: Ignores serial correlation and clustering when computing power.
Gives a number of months without showing how it was computed.
